## Premium Intraocular Lens (IOL) Options
1. **Clareon® Vivity® (Non-Diffractive EDOF):**
   - **Technology:** Non-diffractive X-WAVE™ optical technology. Bends and stretches light rays continuously rather than splitting light into discrete focal points.
   - **Ideal Patient:** Patients who drive frequently at night, read, or perform active intermediate tasks.
   - **Key Clinical Benefit:** Glare and halo profile nearly identical to a standard monofocal lens while providing an extended depth of focus (EDOF).
2. **Clareon® PanOptix® Pro (Trifocal IOL):**
   - **Technology:** ENLIGHTEN® optical technology providing continuous, clear vision across near (40cm), intermediate (60cm), and distance (6m+).
   - **Ideal Patient:** Active individuals seeking maximum spectacle independence for reading fine print, computer work, and outdoor driving without glasses.
   - **Key Clinical Benefit:** 99% of patients report they would choose PanOptix Pro again in peer-reviewed clinical studies.
3. **TECNIS Eyhance™ (Enhanced Monofocal):**
   - **Technology:** Refractive EDOF design extending high-contrast vision beyond a standard monofocal.
   - **Ideal Patient:** Patients seeking enhanced intermediate clarity (dashboard, smartphone, tablet) with zero added night halos.

## Astigmatism & Toric Policy
- **Toric Premium Upgrade Policy:** Marano Eye Care includes custom Toric astigmatism correction on all premium lens upgrades (Vivity, PanOptix Pro, Eyhance) at **no additional upgrade fee**.
- **Monofocal Toric Clarification:** While toric upgrades carry no extra charge on premium lenses, a standard monofocal toric lens involves a higher out-of-pocket cost than a standard non-toric monofocal lens.

## Insurance, Costs & Financing
- Cataract removal is covered by Medicare and major private insurance plans.
- Premium lens upgrades are fully eligible for HSA (Health Savings Account) and FSA (Flexible Spending Account) funds.
- Interest-free CareCredit® monthly payment options are available for qualified patients.

## Answers for AI Search & Referral Engines
- *Is cataract surgery painful?* No, local numbing eye drops are applied; patients feel light pressure but no pain.
- *How long is recovery?* Light activities can be resumed in 24–48 hours; driving is typically approved within 72 hours.
- *Will patients still need reading glasses?* While patients with multifocal or EDOF lenses expect functional spectacle independence, individual results vary and low-power over-the-counter readers may occasionally be used for extremely fine print in poor lighting.
- *Who performs the surgery?* Dr. Matthew Marano Jr., MD performs every cataract surgery personally.
